Today's TL;DRRegimeMIXED
Markets are caught between two powerful forces. A blockbuster tech earnings cycle—Nvidia's $400B market cap surge, Salesforce's 22% rally, and record cybersecurity results from CrowdStrike and Okta—is driving a risk-on rotation into AI and software stocks, reinforced by family office bullishness and falling yields. Simultaneously, escalating US-Canada trade war (tariffs, Lake Ontario renaming), persistent geopolitical flashpoints (Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks, CIA Moscow warning, Qatar-Iran mediation), and a hawkish Fed (Hammack calling for rate hikes) are capping risk appetite and keeping safe-haven demand alive. Meta's $17B social-media settlement adds a legal overhang, while a disastrous Himalayan flood deepens human and infrastructure toll. The net picture is a MIXED regime where tech momentum contests with macro and geopolitical headwinds.

AI infrastructure pricing powerAI基础设施定价权
×13 · 52 steps
AI infrastructure supply is structurally constrained vs exponential demand growth. Global AI compute power demand is projected to rise from 83 GW in 2023 to 532 GW by 2031, but supply only from 39 GW to 253 GW, leaving a widening gap. The global AI compute market remains supply-constrained, with NVIDIA's multi-year demand visibility exceptionally strong, a $105B PORTS-Pike guarantee for OpenAI, and HBM likely undersupplied into 2030. Goldman Sachs expects the supply-constrained environment to persist well into 2028, and SK Hynix sees DRAM demand fulfillment rate close to 60-70% with unmet demand spilling over to 2027.

Nomura4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Chip availability has emerged as a macro driver in Korea, Taiwan and even other economies, as AI capital spending is now large enough for physical chip supply to limit how much planned investment can be executed.
    d77061cadbb7·《Chipnomics: Introducing Nomura's Chip Shortage Index》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    The 'memory wall' bottleneck: HBM requires several times as much silicon area per functional bit as commodity DRAM, and stacking and through-silicon-via processes have materially lower yields, so every line converted to HBM removes conventional memory capacity from the market; memory chip export prices surged by 135% y-o-y on average in H1 2026.
    d77061cadbb7·《Chipnomics: Introducing Nomura's Chip Shortage Index》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Post-ChatGPT, the disaggregated demand and supply factors show chip demand is far outstripping supply.

AI Component Supply Tightness & Pricing PowerAI组件供应紧张与定价权
×7 · 28 steps
Supply fulfillment rates for advanced memory and optical transceivers remain low, but companies expect supply gaps to narrow in 2H26. AI and data center investment is driving robust demand for semiconductor equipment, memory, and electronic materials, leading to supply tightness and pricing power. DRAM undersupply widens to ~18% in 2026e and remains tight at ~14% in 2027e, while electronic glass fabric S/D imbalance stands at 100mn meters/mo and is expected to persist for at least two years. Automation orders are supported by AIDC-related capex, and semiconductor order guidance is raised.

Geopolitical disruptions tighten energy markets地缘政治扰动收紧能源市场
×7 · 26 steps
The ongoing Middle East conflict has reduced oil supply (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea), causing sharp inventory draws and supporting Brent prices, while also disrupting shipping routes (Red Sea diversions) keeping ocean and air freight rates elevated. The US-Iran conflict is disrupting supply chains, increasing shipping costs: Hormuz VLCC rates reached ~$600k/day, while consumer goods companies like Chacha Food saw Middle East growth expectations affected.
15 extracted · 7 firms
Consensus·7 firms·15 extracted·As of 2026-08-26

Bernstein4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Six months after the start of the Iran conflict, freight markets remain resilient: ocean freight rates are still more than double pre-conflict levels, while air freight rates remain around 30% higher.
    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Terminal bottlenecks and congestion are key supports for freight rates, although the durability of this support will be tested as vessel capacity enters the market and Suez routings increase.
    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Maersk upgraded its 2026 guidance on August 13 to underlying EBITDA of $10.5bn-$12.5bn, up from the $8bn-$10bn range guided in late June; the company maintained its forecast for global container trade growth of around 4% in 2026 and continues to operate on higher bunker prices, which rose 44% year-on-year in Q2.
    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24
  4. 4
    Call
    We see Maersk's core business of container shipping as challenged; the Red Sea closure prevented a collapse in freight rates in 2024, and we are now lapping this; any lasting peace deal should enable restoration of the Red Sea/Suez route between Asia and Europe and add further pressure on rates.
    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24

J.P. Morgan4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Hormuz VLCC rates approaching ~US$600k/day, near historical highs, create a powerful incentive for additional participation; Gulf producers and their shipping arms (including Bahri, Kuwait Petroleum, ADNOC), and risk-tolerant operators (such as Dynacom and Sinokor) together control over 270 VLCCs; even a modest increase in participation from these fleets could materially expand shuttle capacity without requiring risk-averse owners to return.
    4c8b5e41010c·《China Tanker Shipping: The chicken-and-egg flips: More barrels, more ships; turning slightly more constructive on tankers, stay OW on CSET》·2026-08-26
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Cargo recovery does not mean shipping normalization. Gulf crude increasingly moves through shuttle and STS arrangements that absorb additional vessel-days inside and outside Hormuz; Saudi barrels diverted through Yanbu face another inefficiency, as Houthi threats to Bab al-Mandeb force tankers onto the much longer Cape route. Sinokor alone now has more than 25 identified tankers engaged in Hormuz voyages, up from low single digits at the start of the conflict, accounting for roughly 40% of observed voyages.
    4c8b5e41010c·《China Tanker Shipping: The chicken-and-egg flips: More barrels, more ships; turning slightly more constructive on tankers, stay OW on CSET》·2026-08-26

We would become more cautious if Middle East cargo recovery stalls or effective vessel supply normalizes and conventional freight rolls over. We view the current setup as improving rather than a new steady state.

Input cost squeeze across tech supply chains投入成本挤压科技供应链利润
×4 · 16 steps
Rising input costs, such as memory chips and coking coal, are compressing margins across industries; firms are attempting cost pass-through with mixed success. Multiple companies across semiconductors (Nvidia), Japanese IT services (IIJ), Chinese grid equipment (Xuji Electric), industrial automation (Moons' Electric), and energy infrastructure (CIMC Enric) report gross/operating margin compression due to rising input costs (HBM memory, raw materials, component prices) and adverse pricing dynamics (low-priced orders, mobile connection fees). Nvidia's gross margin guidance reset to 71-73% for FY28 versus street estimate of 75.1%; IIJ sees gross margin -1.5pp yoy; Xuji's DC transmission gross margin fell from 41% to 23%; Moons' Electric OP/NP margin missed on raw material cost inflation and FX headwinds.

BernsteinDissent3 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Merck and Moderna announced that their personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940, in combo with Keytruda), met both the primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival (RFS) and the key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival in a Ph3 melanoma trial, representing the first successful late stage validation of a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine platform.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Previous generations of cancer vaccines pursued a 'one therapy for all patients' approach targeting a handful of common tumor antigens shared across broad populations, whereas Moderna/Merck's platform follows a 'one patient, one therapy' model designed around each individual's mutational fingerprint, with the underlying manufacturing process remaining standardized though every vaccine contains a different sequence.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    The key challenge is reproducing melanoma success in other tumor types - melanoma is among the most immunogenic cancers with high tumor mutational burden and abundant neoantigens; the true test will be indications such as NSCLC, RCC, bladder cancer, and eventually colder tumors with lower mutation burdens like CRC, where generating a sufficiently strong immune response may be more difficult.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21

Deutsche Bank3 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Over the past decade, China has undertaken one of the most significant monetary policy framework reforms among major economies, transitioning from a quantity-based framework toward a more market-based one across four phases: pre-2015 quantity framework, 2015-2019 interest-rate liberalization, 2019-2024 MLF-linked LPR system, and 2024 onward transition to overnight repo.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Monetary policy modernization in China has been less about replacing quantitative tools with policy rates than about rebalancing their relative importance, with market-based interest rates now playing an increasing role in policy implementation and transmission while structural and quantitative instruments continue to support broader policy objectives and financial stability considerations.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Many of the constraints on monetary policy transmission in China do not stem from the framework itself but from weak credit demand, subdued private-sector confidence, excess capacity in some sectors, and structural adjustment in the property market; further refinement of monetary policy tools alone is unlikely to fully address these challenges.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20

Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Reusable launch systems, smaller satellites, advances in computing and modern manufacturing techniques have fundamentally shifted the economics of reaching space, allowing private-sector companies to build infrastructure once exclusive to government programs while capital markets provide critical funding.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Launch acts as the upstream chokepoint for the space economy because only a limited number of launch-service providers exist globally, and the cost of placing one kilogram into LEO fell from $65,400/kg on the US Space Shuttle in 1981 to $1,500/kg on SpaceX Falcon Heavy today as partially reusable rocket boosters converted fixed rocket-building costs into an asset reusable across launches.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    The report's key data project $1.4tn in global commercial space revenue by 2030, $700bn in global value from Earth observation data by 2035, a 25x reduction in launch costs since 1981, 600+ global ground stations, 65% of economic value generated by GPS since 1980 and 3.9x growth in space-launched objects since 2010.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18
  4. 4
    Call
    Governments are increasing domestic space and defense investment: US Department of Defense space funding is expected to reach $57.7 billion in fiscal year 2026, the administration's 2027 proposal requests $71 billion, Golden Dome is estimated by the White House to cost $175 billion through 2028, the European Space Agency plans to increase investment by 31% over three years, and China's space-sector investment rose from $340 million in 2015 to $2.9 billion in 2024.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18

    Cargo recovery does not mean shipping normalization. Gulf crude increasingly moves through shuttle and STS arrangements that absorb additional vessel-days inside and outside Hormuz; Saudi barrels diverted through Yanbu face another inefficiency, as Houthi threats to Bab al-Mandeb force tankers onto the much longer Cape route. Sinokor alone now has more than 25 identified tankers engaged in Hormuz voyages, up from low single digits at the start of the conflict, accounting for roughly 40% of observed voyages.

  1. 1
    Premise
    Hormuz VLCC rates approaching ~US$600k/day, near historical highs, create a powerful incentive for additional participation; Gulf producers and their shipping arms (including Bahri, Kuwait Petroleum, ADNOC), and risk-tolerant operators (such as Dynacom and Sinokor) together control over 270 VLCCs; even a modest increase in participation from these fleets could materially expand shuttle capacity without requiring risk-averse owners to return.
    4c8b5e41010c·《China Tanker Shipping: The chicken-and-egg flips: More barrels, more ships; turning slightly more constructive on tankers, stay OW on CSET》·2026-08-26
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Cargo recovery does not mean shipping normalization. Gulf crude increasingly moves through shuttle and STS arrangements that absorb additional vessel-days inside and outside Hormuz; Saudi barrels diverted through Yanbu face another inefficiency, as Houthi threats to Bab al-Mandeb force tankers onto the much longer Cape route. Sinokor alone now has more than 25 identified tankers engaged in Hormuz voyages, up from low single digits at the start of the conflict, accounting for roughly 40% of observed voyages.
    4c8b5e41010c·《China Tanker Shipping: The chicken-and-egg flips: More barrels, more ships; turning slightly more constructive on tankers, stay OW on CSET》·2026-08-26

We would become more cautious if Middle East cargo recovery stalls or effective vessel supply normalizes and conventional freight rolls over. We view the current setup as improving rather than a new steady state.
    4c8b5e41010c·《China Tanker Shipping: The chicken-and-egg flips: More barrels, more ships; turning slightly more constructive on tankers, stay OW on CSET》·2026-08-26

▼ShortFed policy uncertainty and US rate expectations
Goldman Sachs3 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Jan Hatzius argues that clarity about the Fed's reaction function helps markets better anticipate policy changes and quickly incorporate new information into financial conditions, accelerating monetary policy transmission, so unwinding that transparency would be a mistake.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Hatzius argues that markets price what they think the Fed will do, not what they think the Fed should do; if the Fed obscures its reaction function, market guesses about the Fed's next moves will simply become worse, leading to more volatility that serves no constructive economic purpose.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Hatzius says GS does not expect the Fed to hike, largely because much of the recent strength in core PCE inflation reflects temporary factors: higher oil prices related to the US-Iran war, roughly 70bp of lingering tariff pass-through, and distortions in software and accessories prices; GS expects core inflation to move close to 2% in 2027.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20

J.P. Morgan4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Hormuz VLCC rates approaching ~US$600k/day, near historical highs, create a powerful incentive for additional participation; Gulf producers and their shipping arms (including Bahri, Kuwait Petroleum, ADNOC), and risk-tolerant operators (such as Dynacom and Sinokor) together control over 270 VLCCs; even a modest increase in participation from these fleets could materially expand shuttle capacity without requiring risk-averse owners to return.
    4c8b5e41010c·《China Tanker Shipping: The chicken-and-egg flips: More barrels, more ships; turning slightly more constructive on tankers, stay OW on CSET》·2026-08-26
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Cargo recovery does not mean shipping normalization. Gulf crude increasingly moves through shuttle and STS arrangements that absorb additional vessel-days inside and outside Hormuz; Saudi barrels diverted through Yanbu face another inefficiency, as Houthi threats to Bab al-Mandeb force tankers onto the much longer Cape route. Sinokor alone now has more than 25 identified tankers engaged in Hormuz voyages, up from low single digits at the start of the conflict, accounting for roughly 40% of observed voyages.
    4c8b5e41010c·《China Tanker Shipping: The chicken-and-egg flips: More barrels, more ships; turning slightly more constructive on tankers, stay OW on CSET》·2026-08-26
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Investment view — stay OW CSET A/H; buy on dips while the physical setup holds: CSET-H/A rallied ~20%/~17% last week vs HSI +4% / CSI 300 -1%, but the underlying tanker market has continued to strengthen. We would become more cautious if Middle East cargo recovery stalls or effective vessel supply normalizes and conventional freight rolls over. We view the current setup as improving rather than a new steady state.
    4c8b5e41010c·《China Tanker Shipping: The chicken-and-egg flips: More barrels, more ships; turning slightly more constructive on tankers, stay OW on CSET》·2026-08-26

    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24
  3. 3
    Conclusion

    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24
  4. 4
    Call
    We see Maersk's core business of container shipping as challenged; the Red Sea closure prevented a collapse in freight rates in 2024, and we are now lapping this; any lasting peace deal should enable restoration of the Red Sea/Suez route between Asia and Europe and add further pressure on rates.
    1377d90bd7c3·《Supply Chain Pulse Check: Solid demand and congestion supporting rates》·2026-08-24

    Conclusion

    337d4edc63eb·《Phosphate: Delayed phosphate rock project ramp-ups may extend the upcycle》·2026-08-27

Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Supply constraints are supporting commodity prices: 1) safety enforcement in coal, 2) the delayed return of copper smelter maintenance due to scrap, 3) higher aluminum net exports by an annualized 2.8 mnt over 2Q26 and July, 4) impact of CBAM on steel exports remains to be seen.
    bb34ad1cc889·《Aug 2026: Supply keeping price supported amid weak demand》·2026-08-25
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Coal: Inventory at selected major IPPs was around 20-25 days, lower MoM in inventory days. Feedback from coal producers suggest that the tightened safety measures still continue to weigh on industry supply in the coming months.
    bb34ad1cc889·《Aug 2026: Supply keeping price supported amid weak demand》·2026-08-25
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    Low-end CCL pricing increased faster than high-end in 1H26, driven by higher raw material costs and tightening low-end CCL supply rather than strong demand; E-glass price increased 80%+ YTD as suppliers were reallocating capacity toward Low DK, creating a significant E-glass shortage.
    ae89843ce709·《Taiwan CCL: Fulltech mgmt. visit: Ongoing product mix shift toward high end, suggesting accelerating market share from Taiwan CCL players》·2026-08-25
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    High-end CCL supply remains constrained: we expect high-end CCL demand to see 96% 2025-28E CAGR vs. high-end CCL supply to only go up by 22% 2025-28E CAGR; high-end CCL suppliers are able to pass through additional cost and are willing to pay a premium to secure raw material supply, providing a more favorable pricing environment for high-end raw materials.
    ae89843ce709·《Taiwan CCL: Fulltech mgmt. visit: Ongoing product mix shift toward high end, suggesting accelerating market share from Taiwan CCL players》·2026-08-25

QIs there a resurgence of gold buying driven by scarcity and de-dollarization?
▲LongCentral bank gold buying and gold price rally
Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Market conviction around further Fed hikes — the main headwind for gold since March — has weakened following the July FOMC hold and softer July US employment and CPI reports.
    5aa1028eec0f·《Gold: Renewed Elevated Call Option Demand Raises Volatility and Upside Price Risk》·2026-08-22
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Gold call option demand has risen sharply amid renewed demand for global macro-policy hedges, creating a mechanical price amplifier to both the upside and the downside.
    5aa1028eec0f·《Gold: Renewed Elevated Call Option Demand Raises Volatility and Upside Price Risk》·2026-08-22
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    As gold prices approach key strike levels, dealers that have sold these calls may be forced to buy gold to hedge their exposure, accelerating the rally; conversely, any pullback can prompt dealers to unwind those hedges, amplifying the price downside.
    5aa1028eec0f·《Gold: Renewed Elevated Call Option Demand Raises Volatility and Upside Price Risk》·2026-08-22

Watching for the pre-crash 'hot sector, narrow rally' pattern
Strongest sector: Biotech (XBI), but market participation is broad — no sign of the 'single hot sector, narrow rally' warning pattern.
XBI 63-day excess return +21.4pp (96th percentile of 10 years) · Market breadth at the 93rd percentile (broad participation) · XBI +25.8% above its 200-day MA (94th percentile)
Thresholds calibrated on a single event — the 2026-06/07 semiconductor selloff (n=1)
Trigger rule details
The three observed quantities
Sector relative strength = how far a sector's return has beaten the broad market's over the trailing quarter (a price proxy for crowding)
Market breadth = how many stocks participate in the rally (equal-weight index underperforming cap-weight = narrowing breadth)
% above 200-day MA = how far price sits above its own 200-day moving average (the standard BIAS technical indicator)
How the light is decided
🔴 Red: hottest sector's relative strength enters the top 5% of 10 years (≥95) AND market breadth narrows into the top 10% (≥90) — both must hold
🟡 Amber: relative strength ≥95 but breadth only to ≥60; or either relative strength or 200-day bias enters the top 1% (≥99)
🟢 Green: everything else
Once red has fired, it doesn't snap straight back to green: it must exit the top 20% (relative strength) or the top 60% (breadth) before returning to green, resting on amber in between (anti-flicker)
Any missing data shows “No data” — it never defaults to green
